title: Love Language #1: Words of Affirmation
coreMove: Affirming words fill the love tank when they are sincere, specific, kind, and humble; praise becomes love only when it builds the spouse, not when it buys compliance.

exampleSpecs.stakes: confidence can grow or collapse before the first submission
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the writer, magazines, encouraging words, and confidence without empty cheerleading

exampleSpecs.audience: couples whose valid needs come out as criticism
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same dinner wish can invite love or start a fight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast a pasta request with a decent meal complaint using humble words

exampleSpecs.audience: spouses unsure when public praise helps
exampleSpecs.stakes: public words can honor a spouse or become pressure in front of others
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use William James, psychologist, appreciation, and human need as the source anchor

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose right words come out harsh
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same sentence can soothe or wound before the door opens
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show tone changing the meaning of a loving sentence

exampleSpecs.audience: couples who reuse old failures during new conflict
exampleSpecs.stakes: an old wrong can become a weapon before the current issue is named
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: frame forgiveness as a commitment not to weaponize the past

exampleSpecs.audience: quiet spouses who feel clumsy with verbal love
exampleSpecs.stakes: silence can look like indifference when the partner needs words
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show a nonverbal spouse collecting and practicing affirming phrases
